SMTO-EXE-0276 — Another window took over before SMTO could type

GUID: f9e09a42-68b8-550c-a061-95d8fd2413dd
Slug: ui-focus-changed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO was about to type or press keys in an app, but a different window came to the front, or a key such as Shift was held down. SMTO stopped so its typing wouldn't land in the wrong place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, close or move away any pop-up, notification or other window that came to the front. SMTO types only into the window it checked, so a different front window stops it.
  2. Don't use that computer's keyboard while SMTO is typing. On Linux, also turn off Caps Lock and Num Lock. On Linux, SMTO won't type while a key like Shift, Ctrl, Caps Lock or Num Lock is active, because it would change the text.
  3. Ask SMTO to bring the intended window to the front, take a new look, and then type again. A fresh check confirms the right window has the keyboard before any keys are sent.

What success looks like

  • The text appears in the intended field of the intended window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer, noting which window kept coming to the front.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Guarded keyboard or visual input was refused because the active window no longer matches the target surface, the target surface is not focused, or (Linux) modifier or lock keys are active in the X pointer state mask.

What this means

  • Desktop input focus changed. Observe the intended window, focus it explicitly, then capture and locate the target again before sending input.

Why this can happen

  • Desktop input focus changed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect fresh capture geometry, surface identity and focus.

How to fix it

  • Bring the intended window forward (for example with ui.focus), recapture and locate the target again, then send the input. On Linux the X query_pointer modifier mask (Shift, Lock, Control, Mod1 to Mod5) must be clear, so held modifiers or active Caps Lock or Num Lock block typing.
  • Observe the intended window, focus it explicitly, then capture and locate the target again before sending input.

Retry and execution caution

  • Observe the intended window, focus it explicitly, then capture and locate the target again before sending input.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh evidence establishes the requested outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
